title: Technology Sector Update for 07/19/2018: DWCH,TEUM,IBM,QCOM,NXPI
text:

Technology stocks still were lower this afternoon, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were slipping nearly 0.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also was falling almost 0.2%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Datawatch Corp ( DWCH ) raced to a four-year high on Thursday, climbing almost 21% to its best share price since July 2014 after late Wednesday reporting a surprise non-GAAP Q3 profit following a 42% year over year increase in revenue. Excluding one-time items, the data-analytics software company earned $0.07 per share during the three months ended June 30, more than trebling its $0.02 per share adjusted profit during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus expecting an adjusted $0.05 per share net loss. Total non-GAAP revenue rose to $12.9 million, exceeding the $11.81 million analyst mean.
In other sector news:
+ Pareteum ( TEUM ) was more than 6% higher Thursday afternoon, climbing past its previous session high that followed the networking equipment company saying it won a $2 million, three-year contract from an unnamed provider of wireless internet services in the rural United States for its mobility enablement software services provided through its Global Cloud Services Platform. The customer also will receive new software capabilities for mobility services to offer their business customers and expanding beyond wireless ISP services into smartphone and mobile services.
+ IBM ( IBM ) was over 3% higher in recent trading, Thursday overcoming a small, mid-morning dip, after late Wednesday reporting Q2 operating earnings of $3.08 per share, up 5% over year ago levels and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue rose 4% year over year to $20.0 billion, also topping the $19.84 billion analyst mean. Looking ahead, the company is projecting operating FY18 net income of at least $13.80 per share, also exceeding analyst estimates by at least $0.02 per share.
+ Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was hanging on to a 1% advance Thursday afternoon, recovering from a slim decline soon after the opening bell, that followed CEO Steve Mollenkopf telling the New York Times its proposed acquisition of NXP Semiconductors is likely caught up in the growing trade war between the Unites States and China. Mollenkopf has set a July 25 deadline to complete the $43 billion buyout bid and he said if the prospective deal falls through, Qualcomm will buy back between $20 billion to $30 billion of its stock. It also will owe NXP Semiconductor a $2 billon breakup fee.
